newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CREDIT OUTLOOK -- Weekly jobless claims.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CREDIT OUTLOOK -- Weekly jobless claims.

text.p: U.S. weekly jobless claims are due on Thursday and analysts said the U.S. Treasury market is vulnerable if claims drop from recent levels.
New jobless claims totaled 340,000 last week and in the most recent week, ended October 5, they are expected to rise slightly to 342,000, according to an average forecast culled in a Reuters poll.
The market has turned bearish, however, following a rally prompted by the Federal Reserve's September decision to keep rates steady and encouraged by weak September payroll data.

"We're certainly in a bear mood here," said Christopher Rupkey, vice president and economist at Bank of Tokyo/Mitsubishi. "People are concerned about the PPI (Producer Price Index) and they are looking for reasons for the market's rally to be halted here."
On Friday, the government will report the September Producer Price Index (PPI) as well as September retail sales.

"We're up near that resistance of early August and all the comments are about what type of bad news it would take to knock the market down," said Rupkey. "Investors are very guarded here. The gains from last week are vanishing."
In late trade on Wednesday, the 6-3/4 percent 30-year bond was down 10/32 to 98-31/32, yielding 6.83 percent.
Early in the session, the bond was up about half a point following good overseas buying.
The 30-year bond yield closed at 6.75 percent on Friday, the day the government reported that U.S. non-farm payrolls lost 40,000 jobs in September.
James Glassman, senior economist at Chase Securities, said the jobless claims data were significant.
"The trend is important because new claims have been down in the 330,000 range and that's quite remarkable," he said.

"The economic news suggests that things have slowed a lot," said Glassman. "Job growth slowed in the third quarter and consumer spending was way off. If that's so, I don't know how jobless claims can be driven down to this level."

Glassman said if jobless claims drop back to the 330,000 level, "that will be a pretty important signal that a lot of this softness in the economy that we've seen must be fairly narrowly concentrated."
Marilyn Schaja, money market economist at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette, said she estimates new jobless claims totaled 340,000 to 350,000 in the latest week.

"The employment numbers indicate some moderation in the strength of the labor market," said Schaja. "I wouldn't get carried away with that notion but in general, the numbers are less strong than they were earlier in the year."
If claims rose to the 350,000 level, the market would respond favorably, Schaja said.
"But then it would start to get nervous about the CPI (Consumer Price Index) next week," she said.
On Friday, the market expects the September PPI to be up 0.3 percent and the core PPI, the index without its more volatile food and energy items, to be up 0.2 percent.
September retail sales are expected to be up a subdued 0.2 percent on Friday. A 0.3-percent rise is forecast for retail sales when auto sales are set aside.
The market is also mulling the possibility that retail sales figures for prior months could be revised upward.
Dealers indicated that Federal funds would open between 5-1/4 percent and 5-3/16 percent on Thursday.
